clue.text: Unfading bloom? In a few weeks nothing’s left for a painter

indicators.note: something left for another is abandoned in favour of it, so one piece makes way for the other

blocks.note: a month is a span of a few weeks
nothing is zero, the letter O
A plus RA, a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter is abandoned within weeks, with nothing left to show.
explanation.walkthrough: In A MONTH the O is dropped and A RA takes its place, giving AMARANTH. RA (Royal Academician) is the standard crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry and legend the amaranth is an imaginary flower that never fades, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Into position, tease cable

blocks.note: first meaning: to persuade or ease something gently into place
second meaning: short for coaxial cable, as used for TV aerials

explanation.surface: Instructions for wiggling a stubborn cable into its socket.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to cajole or gently manipulate, and the noun is the everyday short name for coaxial wiring.

clue.text: Infant crab perhaps, one with turn of speed

blocks.note: first meaning: informal British word for a small child
second meaning: a creature that pinches with its claws
third meaning: something nippy, quick on its feet

explanation.surface: A baby crab scuttling off surprisingly fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for a small child, also anything that pinches, and also something nippy or quick.

clue.text: Homes for wise old birds, low-rise, new-built, energy included

indicators.note: something newly built has been put together afresh, so the letters are constructed in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An estate agent touting new low-rise, energy-efficient housing for wise elderly residents.
explanation.walkthrough: E is included among the letters of low-rise before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are proverbially wise birds, and an owlery is a place where they roost or are kept.

clue.text: Expert manager sporting trench coat

indicators.note: sporting can mean playing about or frolicking, so the letters that follow are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A capable executive turns up wearing a trench coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' looks like 'wearing', but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A technocrat is a specialist put in charge because of technical skill rather than politics.

clue.text: Marianne’s sister extremely eager to install wipe-clean flooring

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters
installing something fits it inside, so the outer letters hold the other piece

blocks.note: the first and last letters of eager
lino, linoleum, is a washable floor covering

explanation.surface: A keen young woman insists on putting in practical kitchen flooring.
explanation.walkthrough: E and R go around LINO to make ELINOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Elinor Dashwood is the elder sister of Marianne in Jane Austen's novel Sense and Sensibility.

clue.text: Grand, far too large home constrained by appalling fuel economy

indicators.note: something constrained is held in and hemmed about, so the first pieces sit inside the last

blocks.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
being in means being at home
one mile per gallon, written 1 MPG with the digit as the letter I

explanation.surface: A grandiose mansion so large that its heating bill is ruinous.
explanation.walkthrough: One mile per gallon is ruinous fuel economy, and the digit 1 stands in for the letter I, a common crossword liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing describes something impressive in scale and grandeur, a stately building for instance.

clue.text: Losing heart, rubbish stored on your premises here?

definitions.note: a phrase describing where things are stored rather than a noun

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, and losing it means that letter goes

blocks.note: garbage is a word for refuse

explanation.surface: Is junk piling up on your property?
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter B of GARBAGE is removed, leaving GARAGE, and the whole clue nods to the junk people keep there.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage is an outbuilding at home where cars and assorted belongings are kept.

clue.text: Magazine regularly feeble on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the spelling is chosen by its sound

blocks.note: feebly, in a weak manner

explanation.surface: A periodical keeps coming across poorly on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A publication issued every seven days is a weekly, and the adverb describes something happening once each week.

clue.text: Removing earth, make big effort to overturn band of rock

indicators.note: removing something takes it out of the word
overturning a word turns it upside down, so its letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to exert oneself is to strive hard
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: Excavation crews strain to overturn a layer of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band of rock' looks geological, but it is a rock group; the first E leaves EXERT before it is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: T. Rex was the glam rock group fronted by Marc Bolan in the 1970s.

clue.text: Greek goddess by herself quietly perfect

blocks.note: per se, Latin for by itself
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
to hone is to refine or perfect

explanation.surface: A goddess making herself flawless in private.
explanation.definitionFit: Persephone was the Greek queen of the underworld, daughter of Demeter.

clue.text: Marksman again tacks back

indicators.note: going back means reading from the end towards the start

blocks.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
tacks are small pins

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter pins up targets for another round.
explanation.walkthrough: RE plus PINS make REPINS, which reads backwards as SNIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a concealed rifleman who shoots precisely from long range.

clue.text: Amazing disinfectant, name curiously covered up

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters are arranged oddly
something covered up is wrapped inside another thing

blocks.note: phenol, carbolic acid, is an antiseptic
the letters of name rearranged

explanation.surface: A marvellous cleaning product whose label is mysteriously hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: Phenol is carbolic acid, a classic antiseptic; the rearranged name slips in just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenal means extraordinary, like a remarkable phenomenon.

clue.text: Serious hope, on and off, to comprehend Irish spelling book

indicators.note: on and off picks letters intermittently, every other one
to comprehend is to take in or include, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: grim means stern or serious
the second and fourth letters of hope
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Hopes come and go of understanding an Irish textbook on spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling book' suggests orthography; it is a book of magic spells. GRIM is followed by O(IR)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimoire is a manual of magic, containing incantations and spells.

clue.text: Pulse so weak, hydrate madly

indicators.note: madly means wildly and without order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor finds a faint pulse and urgently orders fluids for the patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Medically, a thready pulse is faint and fine, felt like a thin thread under the fingers.

clue.text: Domestic animals cross over this?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, read from bottom to top

blocks.note: household animals are pets
a rood is a crucifix

explanation.surface: Cats and dogs step across this on their way in.
explanation.walkthrough: PETS ROOD reversed spells the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pets entering or leaving the house pass over the step at the front entrance.

clue.text: A small Christmas scene completed with minimum of expensive credit

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest part, just the initial letter

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small
a crib is a nativity scene, the manger tableau
the first letter of expensive

explanation.surface: A small nativity set, finished with something costly, bought on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe is to attribute something to a source, as in giving credit for it.

clue.text: Lounge about one luxury resort

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a lounge bar
Roman numeral one
the Ritz hotels are bywords for luxury

explanation.surface: Idling about a luxury holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: B(I)AR is followed by RITZ; 'luxury resort' seems one phrase but the definition is only the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Biarritz is a fashionable seaside town on the Basque coast of southwest France.

clue.text: Classify old stars going supernova?

indicators.note: a supernova is an exploding star, so the letters are blown apart and reassembled

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomer catalogues ageing stars as they explode.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to sort into groups or categories according to type.

clue.text: Apparently soft drinks range catches constable out at first

indicators.note: catching something holds it, so one piece is inside another
at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the Alps are a mountain range
a cop is a police officer
the first letter of out

explanation.surface: A police officer catches someone drinking what look like innocent pop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because these drinks look and taste like soft drinks yet contain alcohol, hence 'apparently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcopops are sweet fizzy drinks resembling lemonade but spiked with spirits.

clue.text: Secure a uniform for horse-drawn carriage

blocks.note: to land a deal is to secure it
taken as written
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Getting hold of a coachman's livery for the carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled coach with a folding top, drawn by horses.

clue.text: Hall proprietor, motorist at first tense, captivated by highway

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before
something captivated is held captive, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: the first letter of motorist
a highway is a road
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A country-house owner, nervous behind the wheel, is enthralled by the open road.
explanation.walkthrough: M is followed by R(T)OAD. The answer fits the surface too: Toad was a reckless motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Toad owns Toad Hall in Kenneth Grahame's children's book The Wind in the Willows.

clue.text: Caught one poking nose in fruit

indicators.note: caught can mean heard, as in catching what someone said

blocks.note: a busybody who pokes their nose into others' affairs

explanation.surface: A nosy person is caught snooping among the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like it means C, but here it means overheard; 'poking nose in' seems to run on, yet 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The medlar is a small brown fruit eaten when softened and partly rotten.

clue.text: Got overlay?

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about whether you have a covering
setter's reading: over and lay become their opposites, under and the past of stand

explanation.walkthrough: Over flips to under, and lay (past of lie, to recline) flips to stood, since lying and standing are opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Got is everyday slang for grasped or comprehended, as in 'I got the joke'.

clue.text: Secret drawer’s opening chest

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of drawer
an ark is a chest or coffer, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A hidden compartment in a chest of drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something dark is to keep it hidden, a confidential matter.

clue.text: Two-thirds failure? Half, when combined

indicators.note: keeping two-thirds of a six-letter word drops its final third

blocks.note: demise is a downfall or collapse

explanation.surface: A puzzling statement about fractions of a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Demi is a prefix meaning half, used only in combination as in demigod.

clue.text: Ability to taste article in dish

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a plate is a dish
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A food critic tasting the item on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A refined palate is a discerning sense of flavour, a gift for appreciating food.

clue.text: One wearing your shirt beginning to mix in two infusions

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its initial letter
in places this letter between, inside the pair

blocks.note: tea and mate, a South American herbal brew, are both infusions
the first letter of mix

explanation.surface: Someone who sports your shirt dips it into two kinds of brew.
explanation.walkthrough: Mate (or maté) is a caffeinated South American herbal drink, made by steeping leaves like tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A teammate plays on the same side, so wears the same kit as you.
